title: MapleStory Classic I/L Wizard Build and Leveling Guide: Lv 30-70
intro: Ice/Lightning Wizards are the fastest mobbing class, with Thunder Bolt hitting up to six nearby mobs. Cold Beam handles tougher targets and can hit through terrain, and Teleport keeps you moving between platforms.

blocks.p: This guide is based off of a realistic lv 70 I/L Wizard build by Grummash.
**Pros**

ul: #4 AoE damage at level 70 in the current COT2 benchmark.
Tied #1 Magic EHP at level 70; tanky against magic-dealing mobs!
Thunder Bolt attacks up to six mobs around the caster, the only 2nd job attack that hits six of any mob.
Cold Beam deals 25% more damage to ice-weak mobs and slows them.
Meditation gives nearby party members 25 Magic Attack.
Teleport keeps you moving between platforms.

blocks.p: **Cons**

ul: Max Thunder Bolt costs 40 MP per cast.
Ice- or lightning-resistant mobs cut the matching spell damage.
Low HP makes a missed Magic Guard buff dangerous.

blocks.p: This guide picks up from our Magician level 1 to 30 guide, which compares these first-job builds by meso cost. Any of them works for an I/L Wizard.
Safer moves 12 SP from Magic Armor to Magic Guard. Grummash's build needs an SP reset; its Cash Shop price is unconfirmed.
Keep the Kerning City citizenship chosen in first job. Its later robe-scroll rewards add LUK or INT, both useful when preparing the level-70 Angel Wings setup.
A training map only works when your attacks connect. Every miss spends MP, wastes the attack animation, and lowers EXP per minute.

blocks.p: Every mob has Avoidability. Fighting above your level raises the ACC needed to hit, while gaining levels closes that penalty. This is why a lower-level map with clean one- or two-attack kills can beat a higher-level map with misses.

blocks.h2: Levels 30-70: I/L Wizard skill build and leveling

blocks.p: Second-job SP cannot be spent on first-job skills, so finish the first-job plan by level 30. Character Builder flags any build that breaks it.

blocks.h3: Cold Beam or Thunder Bolt first?

blocks.p: [[img:f8415b5b8d7c08.png]]Cold Beam hits one mob hard. [[img:e28909e5386b42.png]]Thunder Bolt hits up to six mobs, but deals far less damage to each one. Which to max first depends on how many mobs each Thunder Bolt actually hits.

EXP per minute at level 40 on the best launch map in Training Advisor. On one mob, [[img:24dcca787059a4.png]]Energy Bolt/[[img:5370722a856bb9.png]]Magic Claw 20 hits harder than Thunder Bolt 30, so the Thunder Bolt first column falls back to it.

The break-even is 2 mobs per cast. We max Cold Beam first because most casts do not hit 2+ mobs when they are spread out, while Cold Beam works on every map. Thunder Bolt pulls ahead of Cold Beam if you can consistently hit 3 or more mobs every cast.

Against elemental-neutral mobs, keep using Energy Bolt or Magic Claw as your main attack until Cold Beam reaches skill Lv24 at level 38. Against mobs weak to Ice, [[img:f8415b5b8d7c08.png]]Cold Beam is the better skill from skill Lv18 at level 36.

blocks.h3: Possible changes to the default order

blocks.p: If you consistently hit 3 or more mobs per cast, swap levels 31-40 and 41-50: max Thunder Bolt first, then Cold Beam. At 3 mobs per cast it reaches about 6,222 EXP/min at level 40, against 4,199 for Cold Beam.

Mostly fighting one mob at a time? After Cold Beam 30, take MP Eater 3 at level 41 and max Meditation before Thunder Bolt. Thunder Bolt adds almost nothing on a single target, while Meditation raises every spell, for up to 12% more single-target damage between levels 42 and 55.
Raise Teleport after the first max attack when map movement saves more time than the second spell.

Grummash ends at 299 base INT and 63 base LUK, then gets two more LUK from gear to equip Angel Wings. Do not add base LUK automatically after the total requirement is covered; the leftover AP belongs in INT.

blocks.p: I/L Wizards can hold a shield with either a wand or a staff. Spell cast time does not change with weapon speed, so take the highest M.ATK you can equip. Pan Lid blocks more often than Esther Shield (8.09% against 5.30% Guard chance), while Esther Shield adds 55 MDEF against magic attacks. Every WDEF scroll on the shield raises Guard chance further.

blocks.h2: M.ATK or Critical Rate on gloves?

blocks.p: These numbers use Grummash's realistic level 70 I/L Wizard build and five successful Lesser glove scrolls. Both options use the same five slots.

**+10 M.ATK**
326 to 336 total M.ATK
About 3.07% more expected damage.

**+5% Critical Rate**
9% to 14% Critical Rate
About 1.27% more expected damage.

blocks.note: **Pick Magic Attack.** The five-scroll Magic Attack setup deals about 1.77% more expected damage than the Critical Rate setup on this build.

blocks.p: W.ATK does not increase spell damage. The matching Magic Attack scroll gives twice as much M.ATK as the Critical Rate scroll gives Critical Rate.

**The ratio is the same at every grade.** Lesser gives +1 W.ATK or +1% Critical Rate (+2 M.ATK), Intermediate +2/+2% (+4 M.ATK), Greater +3/+3% (+6 M.ATK), and Chaos +4/+4% (+8 M.ATK). Matching grades have the same success and destruction rates.

blocks.h2: Example builds and Training Advisor maps

blocks.p: Thunder Bolt handles packed maps, while Cold Beam gives stronger single-target damage. Jimmy's budget card uses cheap, clean gear: Energy Bolt with early Meditation, then Cold Beam after an SP reset. A guaranteed kill still works on the weakest normal damage roll with 100% hit rate. Each pick also shows Danger and the nearest potion refill because a small EXP lead can disappear when the walk back is much longer.

blocks.p: **Before you settle in:** The Thunder Bolt picks assume each cast hits every mob in range. Check how many you actually hit during normal movement. If it is one per cast, use the Cold Beam pick. Keep the spell and elemental matchup in your saved build current.

Max Thunder Bolt has 70 Basic Attack with Mastery 10. It can hit six mobs for 40 MP. The skill data lists a 25% electrocute chance and a 2-second stun duration. Lightning-resistant mobs can't be stunned.
**At level 70, the benchmark deals about 6,223 expected total damage to six neutral targets and 7,779 when all six are lightning-weak.**
Max Cold Beam has 170 Basic Attack and Mastery 10 for 22 MP. It slows for 3 seconds, can hit through terrain, and deals 25% more damage to ice-weak mobs. Ice-resistant mobs are not slowed.
**The level 70 benchmark deals about 2,519 expected damage to a neutral target and 3,148 to an ice-weak target.**
Max Meditation gives 25 Magic Attack to nearby party members for 300 seconds. It boosts magical attacks and has no effect on physical Attack Power.

blocks.note: **Level 70 damage check:** At level 70, Cold Beam reaches about 3,148 expected damage against an ice-weak target for 22 MP. Thunder Bolt reaches about 7,779 expected total damage when six targets are lightning-weak.

blocks.h3: Ice and lightning on Victoria Island

blocks.p: Cold Beam has three ice-weak mobs on Victoria Island and eight that resist it. Thunder Bolt has five lightning-weak mobs, and only four resist it.
Weak mobs take 25% more damage. Resistant mobs take 25% less and ignore that spell's slow or stun. The table covers regular spawns from level 20 up.
Aqumander resists ice but is weak to lightning. Switch to Thunder Bolt there. Myewood resists lightning and takes normal ice damage, so Cold Beam is the better spell on it.

MP Eater drains at most once every 5 seconds, and it gets nothing from mobs with 0 MP. On Victoria Island that means Pig, Ribbon Pig, Wild Boar, Ligator, and Fire Boar. Bring extra MP potions for the ice-weak Fire Boars in The Burnt Land.

blocks.h2: Find Your Build's Best Training Map with Training Advisor

blocks.p: **Danger measures how hard a mob hits you for: under 10% of your HP is Safe, 10-24% is Caution, 25-49% is Danger, and 50%+ is Lethal.**
Thunder Bolt usually wins raw EXP on crowded maps. Cold Beam can be cleaner against one ice-weak target. It also works better when a platform prevents six-mob coverage.

ol: Enter the I/L Wizard's real AP and Magic Attack. Add the equipment, shield, current skills, and active buffs.
Check Thunder Bolt at 100% reliability for grouped mobs, then rerun with Cold Beam for single targets.
Read each mob's ice and lightning modifier; weakness adds 25% and resistance removes 25%.
Leave Factor Danger into recommendations enabled. A slightly faster raw map can fall behind when its incoming damage is unsafe.
Choose the one- or two-cast map whose platforms let the selected spell reach its normal target count.
Compare the refill loop. A nearest-town scroll gets you back to town, but you still have to walk back to the map. When EXP/min is close, prefer the map with the shorter walk to potion shops.

blocks.p: Max Thunder Bolt costs 40 MP, so Lemons disappear quickly on six-mob maps. Full Magic Guard adds another large MP expense when mobs touch you: at the basic shop rates, every 100 incoming damage costs about 90 mesos to refill through MG 15, compared with 50 mesos when it stays on HP. Use the Guard level your map actually needs. Buy efficient recovery. Save Magic Potions for a cast breakpoint.
